skill.name: py-observability
skill.description: Observability patterns for Python backends, including structured logging, Prometheus metrics, Sentry error tracking, health checks, and sensitive data redaction.
skill.summary: Add practical observability patterns to Python backend services.
skill.author: CJHarmath

security_audit.summary: Static findings for external commands, environment access, and reconnaissance are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, redaction key names, and request correlation examples. No prompt injection or malicious executable behavior was found in SKILL.md. Semantic review found privacy and information disclosure risks in the Sentry user context and readiness endpoint examples.

remediation.issue: Sentry user context includes a raw email address.
remediation.suggestion: Use a non-personal stable identifier, omit the email field, or hash it before sending events to Sentry.

remediation.issue: Readiness endpoint returns raw dependency exception messages.
remediation.suggestion: Return coarse statuses to callers and log detailed exceptions only to protected logs.

remediation.issue: Redaction examples use a small fixed list of sensitive key names.
remediation.suggestion: Expand redaction coverage for nested objects, headers, bearer tokens, session cookies, and case variants before production use.

semantic_findings.title: Personal Data Sent to Error Tracking
semantic_findings.description: The Sentry example disables default PII capture but then explicitly sets user context with an email address. This can send personal data to a third-party error tracking service unless the team has consent, retention, and redaction controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines import Sentry user context helpers and set the user email explicitly. The privacy risk is clear, although it may be acceptable in some deployments with proper policy controls.

semantic_findings.title: Detailed Dependency Errors in Readiness Response
semantic_findings.description: The readiness check returns raw exception text for database and Redis failures. Public or broadly accessible health endpoints can expose infrastructure details and internal error messages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited readiness endpoint places exception strings directly into response fields. This is a common information disclosure issue when health endpoints are exposed outside trusted operators.

content.value_statement: Python services are difficult to debug when logs, metrics, and traces are inconsistent. This skill provides practical patterns for structured logging, Prometheus metrics, Sentry setup, health checks, and redaction.
actual_capabilities: Shows structlog patterns for JSON logs and request context correlation.
Defines Prometheus counters, histograms, gauges, and a metrics endpoint.
Demonstrates Sentry setup with FastAPI and SQLAlchemy integrations.
Provides examples for health and readiness endpoints in FastAPI.
Includes patterns for redacting sensitive request data before logging.
Gives a checklist for production debugging and feature instrumentation.
limitations: Provides reference patterns, not a complete observability platform.
Examples require adaptation to each application framework and data model.
Does not configure dashboards, alert rules, or infrastructure deployment.
Some privacy examples need stricter controls before use in regulated systems.

use_cases.title: Instrument a FastAPI Service
use_cases.description: Add request IDs, structured logs, metrics, and readiness checks to a Python backend.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Debugging
use_cases.description: Make failures easier to trace with contextual logs, flow IDs, and Sentry events.

use_cases.title: Review Observability Coverage
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to find missing logs, metrics, redaction, and health checks before release.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Logging
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single service module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the py-observability skill to add structured logging to this Python endpoint. Include request context and useful event names.

prompt_templates.title: Add Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the py-observability skill to add Prometheus metrics for this FastAPI route. Include request duration and success or failure counters.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Debugging
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for an incident-prone workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the py-observability skill to instrument this multi-step workflow. Add flow tracing, error context, metrics, and sensitive data redaction.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Observability Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the py-observability skill to review this service for observability gaps. Identify missing logs, metrics, traces, health checks, and privacy risks.

output_examples.input: Add observability to a FastAPI endpoint that submits an assessment.
output: Adds a request-scoped identifier to every log entry.
Records request duration and submission status metrics.
Logs validation failures with user and assessment context after redaction.

output_examples.input: Review a production workflow that is hard to debug.
output: Identifies silent returns and missing failure logs.
Recommends a flow identifier for each multi-step operation.
Adds checklist items for Sentry context, metrics, and health checks.

output_examples.input: Add safe error tracking to a Python backend.
output: Configures Sentry integrations with controlled sampling.
Adds event tags and context for debugging.
Flags personal data that should be omitted, hashed, or redacted.

best_practices: Use stable event names and structured fields instead of formatted log messages.
Redact secrets and personal data before sending logs or error events.
Add metrics and health checks beside the code paths they describe.
anti_patterns: Do not log raw request bodies, credentials, tokens, or authorization headers.
Do not expose detailed dependency errors from public health endpoints.
Do not add high-cardinality labels such as user IDs to Prometheus metrics.

faq.question: What Python frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: The examples focus on FastAPI, structlog, Prometheus, Sentry, and SQLAlchemy patterns.

faq.question: Does it install monitoring tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns that you adapt to your existing dependencies and deployment.

faq.question: Can it help with production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests request IDs, flow IDs, contextual errors, metrics, and checklists for faster debugging.

faq.question: Does it handle sensitive data safely?
faq.answer: It includes redaction examples, but teams should strengthen them for their privacy and compliance requirements.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: Is it a complete observability architecture?
faq.answer: No. It is a pattern library for application code, not a full logging, tracing, alerting, or dashboard system.
